body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed on January 2, 2019 and the Advisory Action mailed on April 8, 2019.
Claims 1-20 are currently pending in this application. By this Amendment,

Applicant amends claims 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, and 19. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims, for example, at paragraph [0035]. Applicant believes that this Amendment adds no new matter.
Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the pending rejections for at least the reasons that follow.

At page 2 of the Office Action, claims 1, 9, and 17 where objected to for a minor informality. This objection is moot by the current amendments to claims 1, 9, and 17. Applicant thus requests that this claim objection be withdrawn.

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1, 2, 4-10, 12-18, and 20, which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 Al) ("Taylor") in view of Mabotuwana et al. ("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Onlin. 2007) ("Mabotuwana") and Walker ("Mesenteric vasculature and collateral pathways" Seminars in interventional radiology vol. 26, 3 (2009): 167-74) ("Walker"). In addition, Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 3, 11, and 19, which were

rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor in view of Mabotuwana and Walker as applied to claims 1, 2, 4-10, 12-18, and 20 above, in further view of Chausiaux et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2018/0192873) ("Chausiaux").
The Advisory Action concedes that further search and/or consideration is

required for the claim features including, at least, "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel, amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomic model, and the received physiological state of the patient" and "calculating a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the determined blood flow demand and a value of microvascular resistance associated with the received physiological state." (Emphasis added.)

Mabotuwana teaches an anatomically and biophysically based model of the major mesenteric arteries to simulate normal blood flows. (Mabotuwana, Abstract, emphasis added.) In so teaching, Mabotuwana neither teaches "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel, amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomic model, and the received physiological state of the patient" nor "receiving a patient physiological state, the physiological state being a state different from a resting state," as claimed. (Emphasis added.) Walker fails to cure the deficiencies of Taylor and Mabotuwana. Walker

simply, broadly acknowledges that "[a] thorough knowledge of both the arterial and venous mesenteric circulation, including normal, variant, and collateral anatomy, is necessary to evaluate and manage various disease processes." Id. Even if Walker teaches of the existence of collateral anatomy, the mere existence of collateral anatomy does not teach or suggest the above-recited claim feature providing a specific method of "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomical model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel, amount of visceral vasculature and collateral pathway(s) supplying blood to the portion of patient's bowel modeled by the patient-specific anatomic model, and the received physiological state of the patient," as claimed. Further, neither Taylor, Mabotuwana, Walker, nor Chausiaux, individually or in combination, teach or suggest "calculating a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the determined blood flow demand and a value of microvascular resistance associated with the received physiological state," as claimed. The Advisory Action is silent regarding how the rejection is maintained with respect to the above-recited claim feature.

As a note, the Advisory Action suggests an amendment to claims 6 and 14 to change "associated with" to "based on" to possibly obviate a future rejection under 35 US.C. 112(b). Claims 6 and 14 do not currently recite "associated with." Applicant requests clarification regarding the Advisory Action's claim recitations.

For the reasons discussed, Applicant submits that claims 1-20 are allowable over all of the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 103 rejections.

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be

entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.
Furthermore, Applicant respectfully points out that the final Office Action

presented new arguments as to the application of the art against the pending claims. It is respectfully submitted that the entering of this Reply would allow Applicant to respond to the final rejection and place the application in condition for allowance.
Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims.
In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against
this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
If the examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 202-803-8075.

Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.
